verdicts.reason: userPermDenialCacheKey joins action, name and parent with bare '_' separators, so (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") produce the same key; pkg/util/shortid_generator.go:33 shows Grafana's UID charset is `a-zA-Z0-9\-\_`, so underscores are legal in both the resource name and the folder UID, and a false hit returns Allowed:false at service.go:117-121.

The denial key is built from checkReq.UserUID before any identity resolution, while getCachedIdentityPermissions/getUserPermissions key on userIdentifiers.UID; GetUserIdentifiers (service.go:463-469) explicitly accepts a numeric ID as the subject, so the same principal can produce two different denial keys and miss its own entries. Effectiveness only — both key spaces hold denials, so no wrong grant results.

NoopCache is only referenced at rbac.go:103 inside its own package (grep finds no other use), the receiver is named `lc` (local cache) on a type that is not a local cache, and the type has no doc comment explaining why the in-proc client must not cache.

getCachedIdentityPermissions repeats the identity-type switch of getIdentityPermissions verbatim, and perm cache keys are now built in three separate places (service.go:348 and 423 for anonymous, 360 and 379 for users, plus 116 for the denial key), so the two switches can drift apart.
Accurate: the key concatenates name and parent with an unescaped '_', and validUIDCharPattern is `a-zA-Z0-9\-\_`, i.e. Grafana UIDs may legitimately contain underscores.

Every denied (user, action, name, folder) tuple writes a new entry, and name/folder come straight from the request (validateCheckRequest copies req.GetName()/req.GetFolder() unfiltered), so the key space is caller-driven and unbounded, unlike the pre-existing per-user/per-action keys. The entries land in the shared LocalCache built at rbac.go:86 with a 10-minute CleanupInterval.

Traced the test with the short-circuit removed: the seeded permCache map is {"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}, so checkPermission returns false, checkInheritedPermissions finds no folders in the empty fakeStore, and the DB fallback (fakeStore with no permissions) also denies — resp.Allowed is false either way, so the assertion never exercises permDenialCache.

SignedInUser.getTypeAndID returns (TypeAnonymous, "0") and (TypeRenderService, "0"), and the subject sent by the client is GetUID() (zanzana/client/client.go:41), so validateSubject yields UserUID "0" for both; the denial key omits IdentityType, so the two principals share denial records. The existing scheme avoided this by using a separate anonymousPermCacheKey and by not caching renderer permissions at all. A cached anonymous denial therefore blocks the render service (which otherwise gets {"*": true} from getRendererPermissions) and vice versa, for up to shortCacheTTL.

Same defect as c001/c005: unescaped '_' between name and parent in userPermDenialCacheKey, with underscores permitted in UIDs (pkg/util/shortid_generator.go:33); a false hit short-circuits to Allowed:false at service.go:117.

The denial short-circuit returns before any cache-permission or DB lookup, and grep shows permDenialCache is only ever Get/Set (cacheWrap has no Delete at all), so a newly granted permission cannot take effect until the 30s shortCacheTTL entry expires — even if permCache is refreshed sooner.

The premise is right — the in-proc service cache really is cache.NewLocalCache(Config{Expiry: 5m, CleanupInterval: 10m}) — but whether authlib's LocalCache caps entry count and whether logically-expired entries are only reclaimed by a 10-minute janitor sweep depends on github.com/grafana/authlib/cache, which is neither vendored nor in the module cache here. Reading that package's LocalCache implementation would settle it.

The comment says "Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked" but the map is {"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}; checkPermission (service.go:558) reads scopeMap[t.scope(req.Name)], which is false, so the seeded entry grants nothing and the test's premise does not hold.

The code answers the question in the direction that makes it worth asking: there is no invalidation path — cacheWrap exposes only Get/Set, nothing calls Delete, and no permission-mutation path touches permDenialCache — so the 30s TTL is the entire contract, which the PR never states.

After the removed case, both remaining test cases in TestService_getUserPermissions set cacheHit:false, so the `if tc.cacheHit` seeding branch (line 365) and the `require.Equal(t, 1, store.calls)` branch (line 388) are unreachable.

The worked example checks out: name="dash1_"/parent="" and name="dash1"/parent="_" both yield the suffix "dash1__", and underscores are valid UID characters (pkg/util/shortid_generator.go:33); the consequence described (immediate deny for up to 30s via service.go:117-121) is what the code does.

The factual premise is correct — the in-proc client now gets &NoopCache{} instead of a 30s LocalCache, so every Check crosses the inproc channel into the service. Whether the remaining server-side permCache keeps the authorizer hot path within budget is a latency question that needs a benchmark or production timings, which are not obtainable from the checkout.

The control-flow description is accurate, but the conclusion is not: falling through to the DB when the cached scope map does not grant is the fail-safe direction, not a risk, and the stale-grant window it complains about comes from permCache's pre-existing 30s TTL (before this PR getUserPermissions returned the same cached map to checkPermission). The change does not introduce the asserted security risk, and the remedy it implies — trusting cached denials — would be strictly worse.

Correct on the substance: the permissionCacheUsage("true") increment sits inside `if allowed`, so a genuine permCache hit that resolves to not-allowed falls through to the unconditional "false" increment at line 137 and is recorded as a miss. (It is a mislabel rather than a double count — only one increment happens per Check, since the counter was removed from getUserPermissions.)

Same collision as c001/c005/c009/c015, stated as a fix: the '_'-joined name/parent segments are unescaped and underscores are legal UID characters, so distinct (name, parent) pairs can share a denial entry and cause false denials.

getTypeAndID returns id "0" for both TypeAnonymous and TypeRenderService, and the denial key is built from UserUID alone with no IdentityType component, so the two identities share denial records within a namespace.

Both halves hold: line 118 records cache_hit="true" for a hit in permDenialCache, not permCache, so one counter now mixes two caches; and line 137 records cache_hit="false" on a path where permCache actually hit but did not grant.
